messages:
maria.chen: Heads-up — I'm scheduling a simulated breach test against the new on‑prem/private deploy tomorrow at 09:30 PT. Quick questions: how do we rotate the KMS key without causing nodes to fail on secret decrypt? also what netpol enforcement level should we flip during the exercise?

sam.patel: For KMS rotation we use an alias switch pattern. Create new key, give it decrypt on the k8s secret-rotation-sa, run re-encrypt job for existing objects, then point alias -> new key. Nodes keep using alias so no downtime. Need infra window for the re-encrypt job. :+1:

elaine_wong: +1 on alias pattern. Important: ensure the offline nodes have current key material cached or they'll hit decrypt errors. We push rotated key material via our secret-agent in two phases: pre-cache -> switch alias -> garbage collect old.

igor_dev: On the netpol side, recommend enforcing egress-deny for app namespaces and allowing only specific destinations (internal registry, KMS endpoint, telemetry sink). During the sim breach flip we can enable a stricter policy that also blocks cloud metadata services. Keep a rollback ready.

maria.chen: Can you paste the minimal netpol we should apply for the test? I want to include it in the runbook.

sam.patel: Sure — example below (apply in staging first):

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-default
  namespace: redwood-private-apps
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8 # internal infra
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          component: kms
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
    except:
    - 10.20.30.0/24 # allow telemetry sink
```

sam.patel: tl;dr: default deny egress, explicit allow to KMS/registry/telemetry.

oncall_bot: Reminder: follow "Private Deploy Simulated Breach" runbook step 3 for KMS alias switch and step 5 for audit log capture. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-sim-breach

maria.chen: About audit logs — do we snapshot the local audit logs and ship to customer S3 or to our central SIEM during the test? Need clarity for evidence.

elaine_wong: Ship to both where possible. Primary: customer-managed S3 (kms-encrypted) via private peering. Secondary: copy to central SIEM (Graylog) over the management VPC. Ensure the shipper uses role-based creds and doesn't leak keys.

igor_dev: One more: RBAC changes. Don't edit clusterrolebinding in place. Create new role with the reduced perms, bind to a canary service account for 10% of pods, monitor 15m, then roll out. If we need emergency revert, we remove binding and restore old binding from the CRB backup.

sam.patel: Commands we usually run for key alias switch: 

```bash
# create new key
aws kms create-key --description "sim-rot-2026" 
# create alias
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/redwood-private --target-key-id <new-key-id>
# re-encrypt S3 objects (example)
aws s3 cp s3://secrets-bucket/ secret-local/ --recursive --sse-kms-key-id <new-key-id>
# update secret-agent configmap to point at new alias
kubectl apply -f secret-agent-configmap.yaml
```

maria.chen: Good. For the simulated breach we also want to intentionally revoke one service account token to test incident response. Any gotchas?

elaine_wong: Make sure the token revocation is scoped — don't revoke the SA used by node kubelet. Revoke the app SA, watch for auth failures, and ensure audit shows the failures. Also make sure audit-log retention is set to at least 30d for the sim evidence.

oncall_bot: Incident channel created: #incident-private-sim-1955554321. Pager duty: sam.patel (primary), elaine_wong (backup).

maria.chen: Thanks all — I'll schedule the 09:30 PT window, add the netpol YAML + key rotation steps to the runbook, and book a 30m pre-window sync with @sam.patel @elaine_wong @igor_dev. If anything else, drop into the incident channel. :coffee:

sam.patel: I'll prep the re-encrypt job and a rollback script.

elaine_wong: I'll validate audit shipping and prepare the SA revocation playbook.

igor_dev: I'll prepare the egress deny policy and a small canary to test connectivity pre/post.

maria.chen: Perfect. Closing thread and moving details into the runbook.

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: run/sim-breach-1955554321 (will not auto-run without manual approval).

maria.chen: Approved, starting at 09:30 PT tomorrow.
